indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B6.4.1.1 Demonstrate understanding of the concept of energy, its various forms and sources and the ways in which it can be transformed and conserved
indicator.objective: Compare renewable and non-renewable sources of energy

skills.description: Explain that renewable energy sources are not depleted when used (e.g. solar, wind, hydro).
Explain that non-renewable energy sources are depleted after use (e.g. firewood, batteries, food, gasoline, diesel, kerosene).
Sort given energy sources into renewable and non-renewable.
Compare renewable and non-renewable sources (e.g. can be replaced vs. cannot be replaced quickly).
Give everyday examples of renewable and non-renewable energy sources used in Ghana.
Explain why it is important to use renewable energy sources.

spec.difficultyPlan: 20 questions total — Difficulty 1: 5; Difficulty 2: 7; Difficulty 3: 5; Difficulty 4: 3.
misconceptions: Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again quickly.
Renewable sources are unlimited in the short term.
Non-renewable sources can be replaced easily.

questions.stem: What is a renewable energy source?
options: An energy source that can be replaced naturally over time
An energy source that cannot be replaced
An energy source that is always dirty
An energy source that is only used once
hints: Think about the sun and wind.
questions.explanation: A renewable energy source can be replaced naturally over time, such as solar, wind and hydro energy.
questions.misconception: All energy sources are renewable.

questions.stem: What is a non-renewable energy source?
options: An energy source that is used up faster than it can be replaced
An energy source that can be replaced quickly
An energy source that is always renewable
An energy source that is never used up
questions.explanation: A non-renewable energy source is used up faster than it can be replaced, such as firewood, diesel and kerosene.
questions.misconception: Non-renewable sources can be replaced easily.

questions.stem: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explanation: Solar energy is renewable because it comes from the sun and is not used up.
questions.misconception: Solar energy is non-renewable.

questions.stem: Name one renewable energy source.
hints: Think about the sun or wind.
questions.explanation: Renewable energy sources include solar, wind and hydro energy.
questions.misconception: All energy sources are renewable.

questions.stem: Name one non-renewable energy source.
hints: Think about fuel for cars or cooking.
questions.explanation: Non-renewable energy sources include firewood, diesel, kerosene, batteries and gasoline.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again quickly.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a renewable energy source?
options: It can be replaced naturally over time
It is only used in Ghana
questions.explanation: A renewable energy source can be replaced naturally over time.
questions.misconception: Renewable sources are unlimited in the short term.

questions.stem: Which statement best describes a non-renewable energy source?
options: It is used up faster than it can be replaced
questions.explanation: A non-renewable energy source is used up faster than it can be replaced.
questions.misconception: Non-renewable sources can be replaced easily.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'All energy sources are renewable.' What is the best correction?
options: Yes, all energy sources are renewable
No, some energy sources are non-renewable, like firewood and diesel
No, all energy sources are non-renewable
hints: Firewood and diesel can run out.
Not all sources are replaced naturally.
questions.explanation: Not all energy sources are renewable. Some, like firewood and diesel, are non-renewable.
questions.misconception: All energy sources are renewable.

questions.stem: Which of these is a non-renewable energy source?
hints: It is used for cooking but can run out.
questions.explanation: Firewood is a non-renewable energy source because it is used up faster than trees can grow.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again quickly.

questions.stem: Give one example of a renewable energy source used in Ghana.
hints: Think about energy from the sun.
questions.explanation: Renewable energy sources used in Ghana include solar, wind and hydro energy.
questions.misconception: Ghana does not use renewable energy.

questions.stem: Give one example of a non-renewable energy source used in Ghana.
hints: Think about fuel for cooking or cars.
questions.explanation: Non-renewable energy sources used in Ghana include firewood, diesel, kerosene and batteries.
questions.misconception: All energy sources in Ghana are renewable.

questions.stem: Why is firewood considered a non-renewable energy source?
options: It is used up faster than trees can grow again
hints: Think about how long trees take to grow.
questions.explanation: Firewood is non-renewable because it is used up faster than trees can be replaced.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again quickly.

questions.stem: A learner lists: solar, wind, firewood, hydro. Which of these is the non-renewable source?
hints: Solar, wind and hydro are renewable.
questions.explanation: Firewood is the non-renewable source in the list. Solar, wind and hydro are renewable.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable.

questions.stem: Which set contains only renewable energy sources?
hints: Solar, wind and hydro are all renewable.
questions.explanation: Solar, wind and hydro are all renewable energy sources.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable.

questions.stem: Explain one way renewable and non-renewable energy sources are different.
answer: renewable sources can be replaced naturally while non-renewable sources cannot
renewable sources are not used up while non-renewable sources are used up
renewable sources can be replaced quickly, non-renewable cannot
questions.explanation: Renewable energy sources can be replaced naturally, while non-renewable sources are used up faster than they can be replaced.
questions.misconception: Renewable and non-renewable sources are the same.

questions.stem: A pupil says, 'Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again.' Is this correct?
options: No, firewood is non-renewable because it is used up faster than trees can grow
No, firewood is a fossil fuel
hints: How long does it take for a tree to grow?
questions.explanation: Firewood is non-renewable because it is used up faster than trees can be replaced.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable because trees can grow again quickly.

questions.stem: Why is it important to use renewable energy sources?
options: They can be replaced naturally and are less harmful to the environment
They are unlimited in the short term
They are only for rich countries
hints: They are better for the environment.
questions.explanation: Using renewable energy sources is important because they can be replaced naturally and are generally less harmful to the environment.
questions.misconception: Renewable energy is not important.

questions.stem: Explain why conserving non-renewable energy sources is important.
answer: because they cannot be replaced quickly and will run out
they are used up faster than they can be replaced, so we need to save them
they are limited and can run out
hints: Think about what happens when they run out.
questions.explanation: Conserving non-renewable energy sources is important because they cannot be replaced quickly and will eventually run out.
questions.misconception: Non-renewable sources can be replaced easily.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly compares renewable and non-renewable sources in terms of replacement?
options: Renewable sources are replaced naturally over a short time, while non-renewable sources take millions of years to form
Renewable sources are replaced over millions of years, while non-renewable sources are replaced quickly
hints: Non-renewable sources like diesel take a long time to form.
questions.explanation: Renewable sources are replaced naturally over a short time, while non-renewable sources take millions of years to form.
questions.misconception: Non-renewable sources can be replaced easily.

questions.stem: A pupil has four energy sources: solar, wind, firewood, diesel. Which classification is correct?
options: Renewable: solar, wind; Non-renewable: firewood, diesel
Renewable: solar, firewood; Non-renewable: wind, diesel
Renewable: wind, diesel; Non-renewable: solar, firewood
Renewable: solar, wind, firewood; Non-renewable: diesel
questions.explanation: Solar and wind are renewable energy sources. Firewood and diesel are non-renewable energy sources.
questions.misconception: Firewood is renewable.
